coverage.category: 3. Second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers
coverage.found: One search. Found only the VAT margin scheme for second-hand goods (ЗДДС чл.143-151) and no Bulgarian police-register or pawnbroker rule. Nothing usable; the police-register question stays unverified.

coverage.category: 4. Gold and jewellery buyers
coverage.found: Dealers in precious metals and stones are in a public register kept by the Ministry of Economy (Валутен закон, since the 2018 amendment), with a separate hallmarking regime. A 2018 draft proposed a register of manufacturer/importer marks and shop signage. Whether it was adopted is unverified. Nothing on the duties of gold buyers who buy from the public. Candidate C2 raised.

coverage.category: 5. Used car parts and vehicle dismantlers
coverage.found: One search. Only drafts and old NAP opinions; no new rule found. Nothing new beyond K03 (waste ledgers) and K05.

coverage.category: 6. Livestock traders, markets and animal transport
coverage.found: One search returned no Bulgarian sources. Only a general EU Reg. 1/2005 outline. Bulgarian registers (БАБХ) not confirmed. Unverified.

coverage.category: 7. Small abattoirs and butchers
coverage.found: The MZH draft ordinance on direct supply of small quantities of food of animal origin (April 2026) would replace the 2010 ordinance. It lifts the geographic limit for poultry and rabbit meat, allows more egg types, and raises the milk-transport time to 48 h. Candidate C3 raised. No new rule for slaughterhouses or butchers specifically.

coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers
coverage.found: Наредба № 10/2015 sets registration and identification of bee colonies. No evidence of an electronic register or new duty in 2025-2026. Nothing found.

coverage.category: 9. Veterinary practices and veterinary medicine sellers
coverage.found: A Bulgarian draft (TRIS notification 26110) adds arts. 61a and 61b to the veterinary medicinal products law: vets must notify antimicrobial use under Delegated Reg. (EU) 2021/578, plus a rule on dispatching prescription-only products (art. 44a). Date unknown. A draft allowing electronic vet prescriptions was also found (undated). Candidate C1 raised.

coverage.category: 10. Well drillers and water abstraction
coverage.found: Owners of wells, boreholes, springs and drains that were not yet recorded had to apply to the basin directorate by 28 Nov 2025 (Закон за водите; municipal notices). That deadline has passed. Permit holders run self-monitoring programmes under Наредба № 1. Candidate C4 raised for permit holders.

coverage.category: 11. Septic, sanitation and waste haulers
coverage.found: Haulers of septic sludge (code 20 03 04) register with the regional environment inspectorate (РИОСВ) under ЗУО. Same buyer group and duty as K03 (НИСО ledgers). Nothing new.

coverage.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors
coverage.found: The DAMTN lift rules (inspection every 36 months per an old source) rest on the maintenance firm and the owner. Condominium managers must notify the municipality of their election, and the national condominium information system (ЕИС) was due 1 Jan 2025 but is delayed. No new lift register or fine found. Candidate C5 raised, weak.

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: EU infringement 2025/2030 (letter of 18 Jun 2025) on Directive 2020/2184 is forcing changes to Наредба № 9. The draft creates an 'individual water source' category and makes the regional health inspectorates (РЗИ) set tap-monitoring points. Duties fall on water operators (ВиК), not on private owners. Nothing for a solo founder yet.

coverage.category: 14. Pesticide and fertiliser dealers and applicators
coverage.found: No search; the spray-record idea is already K02.

coverage.category: 15. Labour contractors and recruitment agencies
coverage.found: Intermediaries register with the Employment Agency under the Employment Promotion Act. A National Council draft would make registration permanent and drop the BGN 120 fee for registering contracts with foreign employers; adoption unverified. Candidate C6 raised, weak.

coverage.category: 16. Cemeteries, burial societies and funeral services
coverage.found: No funeral law; the field is run by municipal ordinances (for example Razgrad Наредба № 10, 2024). A bill on memorial cemetery parks (254-01-122) exists, status unknown. Rules differ per municipality, so a product would need many local variants.

coverage.category: 17. Community and religious bodies: associations, charities, halal and kosher supervision
coverage.found: Non-profits (ЮЛНЦ) must file an annual financial statement in the Commercial and Non-Profit Register. For public-benefit bodies the 2026 dates are AGM approval by 30 Jun and publication by 30 Sep (a blog source). Declarations under ЗТРРЮЛНЦ come with the filing. Accountants already cover this. Nothing about halal or kosher bodies.

coverage.category: 18. Transport operators: minibus, taxi, moto-taxi, small trucking and bus fleets
coverage.found: From 1 Jul 2026, cross-border goods vehicles of 2.5-3.5 t need the G2V2 smart tachograph (an IRU survey page; the rule is EU law). Taxi permits are municipal, and a 2019 dispute over taximeters turned up. The tachograph rule is also on K01's side of the field. Candidate C7 raised, weak.

coverage.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers
coverage.found: Exchange bureaux sit in an NRA public register under Наредба № 4/2003. It was amended by ДВ бр.4/2026 (in force 13 Jan 2026) so rates are set against the euro. The NRA removes bureaux with arrears after a one-month notice. The euro cuts demand for currency exchange, so the market is shrinking. No search on market traders or street vendors.

coverage.category: 20. Small licensed premises with inspections: tattoo studios, driving schools, childminders and nurseries, small food producers, hunting outfitters
coverage.found: Driving schools and training centres: a draft ordinance moves them to electronic documentation, and an IAAA register system holds trainee data. Status unverified. Small food producers: see C3. Tattoo studios, nurseries and hunting outfitters not searched.

result.duty: Claimed duty not shown for Bulgaria. Arts. 61a/61b, where vets notify antimicrobial use under Delegated Reg. (EU) 2021/578, come from the German Tierarzneimittelgesetz amendment (TRIS 26110, BMEL; BT-Drs. 21/1938). That amendment moves annual reporting for dogs and cats to 2029. EU Reg. 2019/6 art. 57 obliges member states to collect use data, with companion animals phased in by 2029. I found no Bulgarian implementing law, frequency or penalty. strategy.bg 7599 is a draft amendment to Ordinance No. 44/2006 on livestock farms. The beta.strategy.bg/download/1046553 file could not be fetched (DNS error), so the e-prescription draft is unverified.
result.market: not_reached. No register count of Bulgarian vet practices or vet-medicine sellers was retrieved.
result.reason: The trigger is not Bulgarian law. TRIS notification 26110 is a German draft, "Entwurf eines Gesetzes zur Änderung des Tierarzneimittelgesetzes und des Apothekengesetzes" (author: BMEL Referat 326). The "/BG" in the URL only marks the Bulgarian translation. The new §61a/61b reporting duty for vets is German TAMG law, and the Bundestag has passed it (BT-Drs. 21/1938, 21/2668). strategy.bg consultation 7599 is about Ordinance No. 44/2006 on livestock farms, not vet antimicrobial reporting. I found no Bulgarian rule in force that makes vets report antimicrobial use or issue e-prescriptions. The EU duty under Reg. 2019/6 art. 57 and Delegated Reg. 2021/578 falls on member states. Bulgaria's own rules and any VetIS (БАБХ) module were not found. Market size and competitors were not reached.

result.competitor: Chekin (automatic ESTI filing at check-in, 14-day trial, connects with 50+ PMS), Hostify (ESTI integration guide), ChargeAutomation ('Bulgaria ESTI Live', sends directly to ESTI), Guesty AutoComply (generates ESTI reports, partly manual upload), Exely PMS (ESTI-ready CSV export, needs the NTR UIN). result.duty: Real. ESTI guest-data entry applies to accommodation listed in the NTR (naredba_esti / naredba_ntr: enter data without delay). Chekin's vendor page says ESTI has been mandatory for all accommodation, including short-term rentals, since 1 Oct 2019, and that failure or delay is penalized; no fine amounts were found. EU Reg. 2024/1028 applies from 20 May 2026 (per a capital.bg snippet; the article itself is paywalled with HTTP 402). Not verified: Bulgarian implementing amendments to the Закон за туризма, which authority issues the number (presumably the municipal categorization or NTR number), and whether a single digital entry point is live. Airbnb's Bulgarian help pages show a 'pending municipal registration' status and let businesses give company details instead of a number.
result.market: not_reached. No NTR or NSI count of class В rooms and flats was retrieved. The capital.bg snippet (Mar 2026) says unregistered listings could be removed under the new EU rules, but I could not read the full article (paywall).
result.reason: The ESTI duty is real. Under the Naredba on the National Tourism Register (NTR), places listed in the NTR must enter guest data into ESTI without delay, and Chekin says late or missing reports are penalized. But the core job is already done by products that target small hosts. Chekin files to ESTI automatically when a guest checks in. Hostify, ChargeAutomation and Guesty AutoComply also claim ESTI filing, and Exely exports a CSV in ESTI format. The registration-number side (how Bulgaria applies EU Reg. 2024/1028 and issues numbers through municipal categorization or the NTR) is a one-off step, not recurring. I could not confirm a Bulgarian law change or a single digital entry point. Micro hosts pay little. Only a narrow Bulgarian-language registration helper remains open.
